observations: Photo 0: Black, horizontal, flat-shaped game console on a wooden stand, front logo area covered by numerous stickers, connected to a Dell monitor showing an Xbox dashboard with an 'Xbox One' style console render as the background art.
Photo 0/1/2: A single black controller with textured grips and a share-button layout (resembles newer Xbox Series controller design) sits in front of the console.
Photo 0: Dashboard shows a few game tiles, including one labeled 'FC26' and another that looks like 'Watch Dogs'; other tiles are too small/blurred to read.
Photo 1: Screen shows live FIFA/FC gameplay (Man City vs Man Utd match), confirming a football game is running.
Photo 2: Screen shows an 'EA SPORTS FC 26' loading screen, confirming this title is installed and can launch.
The console's body is horizontal and flat, not the tall vertical tower shape of an Xbox Series X; this is more consistent with an Xbox One X/S body style.
No visible model label, serial plate, or rear port panel in any photo; stickers obscure most of the top and front surface.
No power brick, HDMI cable origin, or box/accessories clearly shown aside from the monitor's own cable.

identity.kind: Xbox home game console with one controller

claims.evidence: Photo 0/1/2 show a flat, horizontal console body, not the tall tower shape of an Xbox Series X; this looks like an Xbox One X/S form factor, not a Series X.

claims.claim: 6 games installed (FC26, Far Cry 3, Modern Warfare 3, Dishonored 2, Tomb Raider, and one more)
claims.evidence: Photo 0 dashboard shows only a handful of small, mostly unreadable tiles; only 'FC26' and a possible 'Watch Dogs' tile are legible, no full library list visible.
Photo 2 shows the FC26 loading screen and photo 1 shows live FC/FIFA gameplay on the connected monitor.

claims.claim: Far Cry 3, Modern Warfare 3, Dishonored 2, Tomb Raider installed
claims.evidence: None of these titles appear in any legible tile or screen across the 3 photos.

risks.risk: True console model (Xbox One X vs One S vs Series S/X) materially changes resale value and is not confirmed by any visible label.
risks.proof: Clear photo of the rear port panel and/or the official model sticker/serial plate on the underside of the console.
risks.if_unproven: priced as the lower-value Xbox One X tier, not as a Series console

risks.risk: Storage capacity (which affects how many games can be kept installed) is unknown.
risks.proof: Screenshot of the console's storage/settings menu showing total and free space.
risks.if_unproven: priced at base/lowest common capacity for that model

risks.risk: Games may be tied to a Game Pass subscription or a signed-in account rather than being owned/purchased outright, meaning they could vanish after resale.
risks.proof: Screenshot of 'My games & apps' with purchase/ownership status, or Xbox account purchase history.
risks.if_unproven: priced as console-only value, games treated as not conveyable

risks.risk: Extensive stickers may be hiding scratches, cracks, or heat damage on the console shell.
risks.proof: Photo of the console with all stickers removed, or at minimum additional angles of the top and sides.

risks.risk: No power adapter, HDMI cable, or original box shown, and only one controller is visible.
risks.proof: Photo laying out all included accessories: power cable, HDMI cable, controller(s), box.
risks.if_unproven: priced as console + single controller only, no extra accessories included

risks.risk: Internal hardware condition (fan noise, overheating, disc drive if any) cannot be assessed from photos.
risks.proof: Short video clip of the console powering on, running a game for a minute, and showing fan noise level.
risks.if_unproven: priced as functionally unverified, worst-case 'as-is' condition

proof_requests: Clear photo of the rear port panel and the model/serial sticker on the console's underside.
Screenshot of 'My games & apps' showing full list of installed titles and their ownership/Game Pass status.
Photo of console with stickers removed or additional unobstructed angles of the shell.
Photo of all included accessories (power brick, HDMI cable, controller(s), box).
Short video of the console booting and running a game to confirm functionality and fan noise.
response.reason: The item is clearly a Microsoft Xbox home console with one controller, but the seller's 'Series 1x' label is contradicted by the flat horizontal body shown in all three photos (more consistent with an Xbox One X/S), and only one of the claimed six games (FC26) is actually confirmed on screen, so it must be priced at the lower-tier model with unverified extra games and hidden-condition risk under the stickers.
